{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Japan|Cuisine of Japan]]

'''''Okonomiyaki''''' is a popular savory pancake dish in Japan. It consists of a batter made of flour, eggs, cabbage and green onions and other ingredients of your choice. The name means "as you like it" or "what you want" in Japanese. 

== Ingredients ==

=== Base ===
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] all-purpose [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] (or [[Cookbook:Yam flour|yam flour]] if you can get it) 
* 1 cup water (or [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]])
* 2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* ¾ cup finely [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]] (about 2 inches long by ¼ inch wide)
* 2–3 [[Cookbook:Green Onion|green onions]], chopped into ¼" rounds (use white part and freshest bit of green part)
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Mozzarella Cheese|mozzarella cheese]] (optional; other [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]] may be substituted)
* 10 small slices of [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]] or [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] (your choice)

=== Toppings ===
* Okonomiyaki sauce (sold at Japanese markets)
* Dried [[Cookbook:Bonito Flakes|bonito flakes]]
* Powdered [[Cookbook:Nori|nori]] (seaweed)

== Procedure ==  

# Mix flour, water and eggs until smooth (about 25–30 strokes with a spoon or [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]]; do not overmix.) 
# Gently [[Cookbook:Folding|fold]] in cabbage, green onions and cheese. 
# Heat a [[Cookbook:Griddle|griddle]] or [[Cookbook:Non-stick|non-stick]] [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] over medium heat. When pan is hot, add 1 tablespoon oil.  
# Add ⅓ cup of batter and flatten slightly. [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] for 2–3 minutes.
# When pancake is golden brown on bottom, add toppings (chicken, bacon or beef, or other topping of your choice), and press into the batter slightly. Turn the pancake and fry for five minutes or until golden brown on other side.
# Turn once more and fry topping side up for another minute.
# To serve, place the ''okonomiyaki'' on a plate, top with bottled sauce, nori, and/or bonito flakes. Enjoy!
